title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We have hubs in the Bay Area, NYC, Austin, Toronto, and São Paulo. However, we maintain a remote-first work culture. #WorkFromAnywhere

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

Location:

  • Remote - Germany

  • From Home / Beach / Mountain / Cafe / Anywhere!

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed team. You can find your productive zone and work from there.

About the Role:

As a DevOps Engineer at Sardine, you'll play a critical role in evolving our infrastructure and platform tooling to support a growing engineering team. This is a hands-on, high-impact role where you’ll drive key initiatives across deployment, observability, developer productivity, and cloud cost management.

You’ll work closely with application engineers, QA, and cross-functional stakeholders like Security and Finance to ensure our systems are reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient. The role involves building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, improving system observability, optimizing cloud usage through FinOps governance, and strengthening our platform’s resilience. While we have core tools in place, we’re looking for someone who can both own and elevate them by identifying gaps, improving automation, and proactively driving improvements.

This is an ideal role for someone who brings deep technical expertise, thrives in high-ownership environments, and is excited to shape the future of DevOps.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own and evolve our DevOps and platform engineering function, from build and deployment pipelines to monitoring, infrastructure as code, and cost optimization.

  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines that are secure, scalable, and built to support rapid product iterations without sacrificing stability.

  • Improve observability via Datadog, GCP, and custom dashboards, including FinOps focused observability outcomes.

  • Implement and maintain FinOps governance, including showback and chargeback models, to drive cost accountability across engineering teams.

  • Enable developer productivity by creating internal tooling, reusable modules, and simplifying infrastructure for other engineering teams.

  • Help teams define and measure SLOs setting the standard for how we think about system health and reliability.

  • Serve as a FinOps thought leader, collaborating with Product and Engineering to define the most cost-effective architectural patterns for new services and features.

  • Play a key role in shaping our engineering culture, DevOps best practices, and influencing our long-term DevOps roadmap.

  • Work cross-functionally with product engineering, security, finance, and other teams to align technical spending with business unit economics and financial goals.

What you'll need:

  • 6+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or software engineering roles, ideally in high-growth startup environments

  • Proficiency in Python or Go, with strong software engineering fundamentals

  • Proven ownership of production infrastructure and platform tooling, with strong debugging skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex distributed systems and diagnose unforeseen financial spikes

  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing highly secure and robust infrastructure, particularly in environments with stringent regulatory requirements such as those used by government agencies and major financial institutions

  • Deep experience with Kubernetes and tools like ArgoCD, Helm, and Terraform

  • Familiarity with GCP (preferred) or other major cloud providers, with a deep focus on cloud cost management, leveraging reserved instances/savings plans, and implementing cost anomaly detection

  • Hands-on experience with dedicated FinOps tooling (e.g., Kubecost, AWS Cost Explorer, GCP Cloud Billing, DoIT Cloud Intelligence) or building custom tooling for cost allocation and reporting.

  • Strong experience building CI/CD pipelines and internal developer tooling from the ground up

  • Hands-on experience with observability tools like Prometheus or Datadog, and participation in an on-call rotation

Benefits we offer:

  • Generous compensation in cash and equity

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

About

Linro is a cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro.

Cloud infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making those changes, not people. Most security tools only catch problems after the fact. Linro works differently. You would be one of our first engineers, building alongside the founding team. At the heart of the product is a stream-first policy engine that evaluates compliance as SQL across past, present and future infrastructure state. It has to be fast, correct and impossible to route around. You'd own large parts of it outright.

What you will do

  • Design and build core backend services in Go that evaluate policy against cloud infrastructure changes in real time.

  • Take a core area of the platform and own it end to end, from first design through running it in production.

  • Build the simulation and enforcement path that blocks or auto-remediates non-compliant changes before they reach production.

  • Stay close to customers, see how your work lands in the real world, and fold what you learn back into the product.

What we are looking for

  • Strong backend engineering experience in a compiled, statically typed language. We build in Go, so you are either already a Go engineer or someone who will get into it quickly.

  • You know SQL well and think naturally in relational and columnar data models. It’s central to how our engine works.

  • A product mindset. You care about the user and the problem, not only the ticket, and you have opinions about what to build, not just how.

  • A problem-to-solution instinct. You can take an ambiguous problem, find the simple core, and ship something that solves it.

  • End-to-end ownership. You own a problem from design through production and operation, and you see the hard parts through.

  • Hands-on experience operating and running at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP or Azure). Not just deploying to it, actually running it: access management, networking or the failure modes.

  • Hands-on with Terraform or Pulumi, and an understanding of how infrastructure-as-code actually behaves in practice.

  • You build with AI coding tools as a normal part of your workflow and have a point of view on where they help and where they don't. We build guardrails for these tools, so we want engineers with deep, hands-on experience in agentic development.

Nice to have

  • Background in cloud or cyber security, CSPM, CNAPP, or compliance (e.g. SOC 2, PCI, ISO 27001, GDPR).

  • Experience building policy or rule engines.

  • Experience with high-availability, scaling, and eventually-consistent, event-driven system design.

  • Production experience running Kubernetes clusters.

  • Early-stage startup experience, or having been a founding engineer before.

How we work

We are remote across Europe and hire anywhere within roughly two hours of Central European Time (CEST). We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time.

What we offer

  • Real ownership. As an early engineer you design, ship, run and own a genuine surface area of the product, with direct contact with users and a say in how we build.

  • Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it.

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market.

  • A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other’s time seriously.

The honest version

This is early. Priorities will shift, and some of what you build early will change as we learn. There is no playbook waiting for you. If you want a highly structured environment with a mature codebase and a clear roadmap for the next two years, this is not it. If you want to shape a product and a category from close to the start, and you like the idea of building the thing that keeps AI agents from breaking production, we should talk.

Your mission

As our Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem, you will define the product what and why for how ProGlove devices connect, integrate and create value within the enterprise Android ecosystem.

ProGlove is evolving from a wearable scanner company into a Worker Companion company, bringing together ergonomic wearable hardware, software, connectivity, workflow guidance, data and intelligence. With the MAI Wearable Companion, we are entering a broader ecosystem of enterprise applications, technologies, standards, partners and customer infrastructure.

Your mission will be to make our products easy to adopt, integrate and deploy at scale – without turning every customer opportunity into a bespoke engineering project. You will identify recurring customer needs, translate them into scalable capabilities and propositions, and decide where ProGlove should own, enable or partner. In doing so, you will help turn integration from a technical necessity into a source of differentiation, customer value and commercial opportunity.

You will work closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion device. While they own the device proposition, you will own how the device connects to and creates value in the wider ecosystem. Together, you will shape a coherent end-to-end proposition for customers, developers, integrators and partners.

Your day-to-day 
  • Define and evolve the product strategy and priorities for ProGlove’s enterprise Android integration and ecosystem capabilities, aligned with customer needs and business goals.
  • Work directly with customers, Sales and Solution Architecture to identify recurring problems, distinguish individual requests from broader market needs and turn the right opportunities into scalable solutions.
  • Translate recurring integration needs into repeatable product capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, tools, interfaces, documentation, integration patterns and deployment solutions.
  • Shape the product experience around device setup, provisioning, application distribution, device management and other capabilities required to deploy and operate connected device fleets at scale.
  • Make clear, pragmatic decisions about where ProGlove should own, enable or partner, balancing customer value, strategic control, speed, scalability and technical complexity.
  • Identify the platforms, applications, standards and ecosystem players that matter to our customers, and shape the integrations, certifications and technology partnerships that strengthen our proposition.
  • Explore where integration capabilities, software, services and ecosystem propositions can create differentiated value and support commercial or recurring-revenue opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering and the Product Manager for the Wearable Companion to create alignment on customer problems, priorities, trade-offs and desired outcomes.
  • Enable Sales and other customer-facing teams to clearly explain our Android proposition, supported capabilities, integrations and common deployment patterns.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of enterprise Android, AOSP, enterprise mobility, AI and adjacent technologies, and translate relevant developments into strategic options and product priorities.


Your profile

At ProGlove, technical expertise matters, but how you work is just as important. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays curious, collaborates openly and turns complexity into clear, pragmatic decisions.

  • You bring strong Product Management experience in B2B or enterprise technology and can define strategy, discover meaningful customer problems, prioritize opportunities and turn them into scalable products or propositions.
  • You are commercially minded and naturally connect product decisions with customer value, differentiation, business impact and opportunities to capture value.
  • You are comfortable working with enterprise software, platforms, connected devices, integrations or technology ecosystems, and understand the realities of complex customer IT environments.
  • You have enough technical depth to understand architecture, interfaces and trade-offs, contribute credibly to platform and integration discussions, and recognize when deeper engineering expertise is needed.
  • You think in systems and patterns: when faced with a customer requirement, you look beyond the immediate request to understand why it exists, how broadly it applies and what a simple, repeatable solution could look like.
  • You take end-to-end ownership, move topics forward without waiting for perfect instructions and remain effective when the product space or path ahead is not yet fully defined.
  • You collaborate generously and build trust across Product, Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture, customers and external partners. You can create alignment and drive decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • You communicate clearly and transparently, raise risks early and can make complex technical and commercial topics understandable to different audiences.
  • You are curious about customers, the business and emerging technologies, and continuously test assumptions rather than pursuing technology for its own sake.
  • You use pragmatic judgment to balance speed, simplicity, quality and long-term value.
  • You are fluent in English and comfortable working in an international environment.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable, but is not required:

  • Enterprise Android, AOSP or adjacent Android ecosystems, including environments operating outside standard Google Mobile Services.
  • Enterprise mobility management, MDM/EMM, device provisioning, application deployment or connected fleet management.
  • Rugged or industrial devices, IoT or edge devices, connected hardware or other B2B technology ecosystems.
  • APIs, SDKs, developer or integrator experiences and enterprise integrations.
  • Platform or ecosystem strategy, technology partnerships, certification programs or developer and partner ecosystems.
  • Enterprise customers deploying technology at scale.
Direct Android Product Management experience is an advantage, but not essential if you bring strong Product Management expertise and relevant experience from an adjacent enterprise technology ecosystem.


Why us?

This is an opportunity to shape an important part of a category that is still being defined. 
Android gives ProGlove access to a much broader technology ecosystem, but the opportunity goes far beyond compatibility. You will help determine what role ProGlove should play in that ecosystem, which capabilities we should own, where we should partner, what customers and developers should be able to build around us, and where integration itself can become a source of differentiation and recurring business value. 
ProGlove already has the customer base, market credibility, technology and industrial expertise to build on. Our products are used in some of the world's most demanding operational environments. What we are now building is the next layer. 
Over time, success will mean more than making our own products easier to integrate. It will mean creating capabilities, interfaces and ecosystem relationships that customers, application providers and partners actively choose to build around - moving ProGlove from ecosystem participant toward ecosystem shaper. 
If you are excited by the idea of turning complex technology ecosystems into simple, valuable products - and helping shape how the next generation of frontline technology connects with the digital world - we would love to meet you. 
Join us in building the future of frontline work.

This is a highly cross-functional role. description:
About the team:

The Commercial Systems and Intelligence squad is a newly formed team within SumUp's Acquisition Mission under the Run & Grow tribe. We sit at the intersection of data, backend engineering, and sales operations, building the infrastructure that powers how SumUp attributes merchant acquisition, calculates commissions, and understands the full lifecycle of every merchant.

Today, these processes are largely manual. We're here to change that, automating what's opaque, and building systems that sales representatives, leadership, and analysts can actually trust. What you'll do:

  • Aggregating data from across the SumUp ecosystem to determine which acquisition channel or sales agent drove a merchant to take a valuable action (e.g. signing up, adopting a product)

  • Build the Lifecycle Event Log in close collaboration with the Merchant Intelligence squad. A centralized store of curated merchant lifecycle events (signups, product usage, verification, purchases) used across attribution, recommendations, customer support and sales
  • Build internal backoffices and APIs for sales representatives and leaders to monitor commission and modify commission plans, manage portfolios and resolve disputes
  • Define and document API contracts, schemas, and integration patterns that other engineering teams can adopt confidently
  • Establish best practices for testing, observability, and incident response within a newly formed squad
  • Use AI and agentic coding tools deliberately, to scaffold services, write tests, explore unfamiliar code, and draft documentation while maintaining full accountability for what gets shipped

 

You'll be great for this role if you:

  • Bring a strong backend engineering background in Go, or are a typed-language generalist ready to ramp up quickly
  • Have designed APIs and distributed systems with clear contracts, versioning, and integration patterns
  • Are fluent in relational and analytical databases (PostgreSQL, Snowflake) and comfortable making the right choice for the right use case

description:
Bau mit mir das erfolgreichste Beratungsunternehmen der Automobilbranche.

Du willst nicht nur in einem erfolgreichen Unternehmen arbeiten. Du willst mitgestalten, wie groß es wird.

Du denkst unternehmerisch, verstehst digitale Prozesse und willst mit KI wirklich etwas aufbauen? Dann entwickle direkt mit mir unser Unternehmen weiter – und baue dir dabei deinen eigenen Verantwortungsbereich auf.

Ich bin Sascha Röwekamp, Gründer von RWKMP®. Unsere Grundlage steht: fünf Jahre am Markt, 2026 bereits über zwei Millionen Euro Umsatz, mehrere hundert Coachingteilnehmer und Kunden in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz. Mit CARvinci haben wir außerdem eine eigene KI-Lösung für die Automobilbranche aufgebaut.

Unser Ziel: Wir wollen selbst vorleben, wie eine Unternehmensberatung mit intelligenten Prozessen und KI außergewöhnliche Kundenerlebnisse schafft. Was du dafür bei uns entwickelst, kann anschließend zum Vorbild für große Autohausgruppen werden.

Du arbeitest nicht an einem isolierten Digitalisierungsprojekt. Du entwickelst die Abläufe, mit denen wir wachsen – und kannst das daraus entstehende Wissen in eine ganze Branche tragen.

Aufgaben

  • Coachingprogramme organisatorisch verantworten: Du steuerst unsere zwölfmonatigen Programme vom Onboarding bis zum Abschluss: Teilnehmer, Gruppen, Termine, Kommunikation, Unterlagen sowie Zugänge zu Learning Suite und CARvinci. Unsere Kunden sollen nicht hinter Informationen herlaufen müssen.
  • Prozesse verstehen und automatisieren: Du entwickelst unsere bestehenden Systeme mit Airtable, Make, n8n, Claude und ChatGPT weiter. Beispiel Welcome-Paket: einmal selbst packen, anschließend den automatisierten Versand über einen Dienstleister aufbauen – inklusive Versandkontrolle.
  • KI-Anwendungen verbessern: Gemeinsam mit dem Coachingteam entwickelst du unseren KI-Coach und Voicebots für Telefonakquise-Übungen weiter. Du machst Kundenfeedback aus Managementgesprächen systematisch auswertbar, damit das Team erkennt, wo Unterstützung gebraucht wird.
  • Live-Trainings begleiten: In Münster koordinierst du Unterlagen, Namensschilder, Raum und Technik und packst selbst mit an. Morgens Technik anschließen, später mit einem Geschäftsführer über digitale Prozesse sprechen: Genau diese Mischung gehört zur Stelle.
  • Wachstum mitgestalten: Direkt mit der Geschäftsführung setzt du Digitalisierungsprojekte um. Perspektivisch entwickelst du internationale Abläufe oder neue KI-Angebote für unsere Kunden mit.
  • Du musst weder verkaufen noch selbst Coachings geben. Dein Schwerpunkt bleibt die Verantwortung für unsere Operations. Zuerst übernimmst und verbesserst du bestehende Abläufe. Darauf baust du zusätzliche Verantwortung auf – nicht alles gleichzeitig.

Deine Perspektive: einen eigenen Bereich aufbauen.

Du arbeitest unmittelbar mit mir sowie unseren Verantwortlichen für Sales und Coaching. Wir vereinbaren Ziele und Prioritäten. Du entwickelst Lösungen, wählst passende Tools aus und verantwortest die Umsetzung zunehmend eigenständig.

Dass daraus mehr werden kann, zeigt Constantin Michel: Vor fünf Jahren als Werkstudent gestartet, ist er heute mit 25 geschäftsführender Gesellschafter unserer KI-Firma hinter CARvinci. Das ist keine garantierte Laufbahn – aber ein konkretes Beispiel dafür, wie viel Verantwortung hier möglich ist.

Deine Perspektive kann zum Head of Operations mit Budgetverantwortung und eigenen Mitarbeitern führen. Entscheidend ist, was du aufbaust und wie sich RWKMP entwickelt.

Qualifikation

Du kannst einen Workflow bauen und einem Geschäftsführer erklären, warum er wirtschaftlich sinnvoll ist.

  • Praktische KI-Erfahrung: Du hast mit Claude und ChatGPT gearbeitet, einen eigenen GPT oder vergleichbaren Assistenten eingerichtet und erste Automatisierungen gebaut oder getestet – beispielsweise mit Make oder n8n.
  • Analytisches Denken und Umsetzungskraft: Du verstehst wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge, beherrschst Excel und machst aus einer Idee eine funktionierende Lösung.
  • Außergewöhnliche Struktur: Du behältst parallele Programme und Termine im Blick, hältst Zusagen nach und testest Abläufe, bevor Kunden damit arbeiten.
  • Eigenverantwortung und Kommunikation: Du klärst Fragen professionell, meldest Probleme frühzeitig und gehst konstruktiv mit direktem Feedback um. Auch operative Routine und praktisches Anpacken gehören für dich dazu.

Ein Studium in BWL, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Digital Business oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich ist eine gute Grundlage, aber keine Voraussetzung. Entscheidend sind dein Können, dein Anspruch und deine Umsetzungskraft – nicht allein dein Abschluss. Automobilwissen brauchst du zum Einstieg nicht.

Benefits

  • Gestaltungsspielraum statt langer Freigabewege: Du darfst Prozesse verändern, passende Software auswählen und neue Lösungen umsetzen. Entscheidend sind nachvollziehbare Ergebnisse und ein verantwortungsvoller Umgang mit Daten und Budget.
  • Weiterbildung nach Bedarf statt nach Restbudget: KI-Ausbildungen, Automatisierung, Projektmanagement und persönliche Entwicklung. Sag uns, was du brauchst und wofür. Ein sinnvoller Kurs scheitert nicht an einem aufgebrauchten pauschalen Jahresbudget.
  • Ausstattung, die zu deiner Arbeit passt: Premiumzugänge zu benötigten KI-Tools, MacBook oder Windows-Laptop, Firmenhandy, klimatisiertes Büro und höhenverstellbare Schreibtische. Dazu Firmenfitness, PrepMyMeal und Getränke.
  • Langfristige Zusammenarbeit und Zeit außerhalb des Jobs: Unbefristete Position, 30 Tage Urlaub plus Geburtstag frei und 1–2 Tage Homeoffice nach Abstimmung. An Live-Trainingstagen bist du in Münster. Regelmäßige deutschlandweite Dienstreisen und Hotelübernachtungen gehören nicht zum normalen Arbeitsalltag.

Dein Einstiegsgehalt innerhalb der genannten Spanne richtet sich nach deinen Fähigkeiten und der Verantwortung, die du bereits eigenständig übernehmen kannst.

Wenn du groß denken und selbst umsetzen willst, möchte ich dich kennenlernen.

Sascha Röwekamp
Gründer von RWKMP®
